prompt:
You are a decision-support tool for a radiologist. Review this patient's frontal chest X-ray and report on six findings. A radiologist checks your output; give your best assessment. Findings and their definitions: - Lung Opacity: airspace opacity, consolidation, infiltrate or airspace disease in the lung. A discrete nodule or mass is not Lung Opacity (it is Lung Lesion). - Cardiomegaly: an enlarged heart. A borderline or upper-normal heart size counts as absent. - Atelectasis: collapse or incomplete expansion of lung tissue, including subsegmental or plate-like atelectasis. - Lung Lesion: a nodule, mass or cavity in the lung. A calcified granuloma does not count. - Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space. - Fracture: a fracture of the ribs, clavicles, spine or any other visible bone. Healed or old fractures count. How to work: 1. Read the patient's image systematically first. 2. Then look at the 10 most similar cases from a reference database, listed below with their reports. They are other patients whose images look similar to this one. Use them as supporting evidence to confirm or question what you see in the patient's image, not as the answer: a finding in a similar case does not mean that this patient has it. 3. For each of the six findings, give its status (present, absent or uncertain), the probability (0 to 1) that it is present in this patient, the IDs of the similar cases that support your call (an empty list if none), and a rationale of one or two sentences. Then give a short impression. Do not explain what the findings are. Cite cases by their ID exactly as written, e.g. CXR316. Give the probability with two decimals as your honest estimate; for subtle, borderline or partly obscured appearances, use intermediate values rather than a fixed low value. findings.rationale: The lung fields are clear bilaterally without any evidence of focal consolidation or airspace disease. This is consistent with multiple similar cases reporting clear lungs.
The cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits for size and contour. All referenced similar cases also report a normal heart size.
No linear opacities or signs of lung volume loss are identified. Clear lung findings in similar cases support the absence of atelectasis.
No nodules or masses are observed; although similar cases mention calcified granulomas, these do not meet the definition for Lung Lesion.
The costophrenic angles are sharp and well-defined, indicating no pleural fluid accumulation. This observation is supported by several similar negative cases.

The visible osseous structures, including the ribs and clavicles, appear intact without evidence of acute or old fracture. Minimal degenerative changes in the spine are noted but do not constitute a fracture.

parsed.impression: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality; normal heart size and clear lungs.
